newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA says inflation, wages key to rates.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA says inflation, wages key to rates.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) said in its quarterly Bulletin that low inflation expectations would support a case for lower interest rates.

However, the RBA also said interest rate cuts depended on wages growth, and said some wage agreements were based on higher than actual inflation. It said a case for lower rates would be strengthened if the economy was weaker than expected.
The bank said the economy may grow a litle faster without the threat of inflation, depending on wages.
The bank said it was disappointed that some wage agreements had been based on higher than actual inflation levels.

"Excessive wage agreements adversely affect growth and employment prospects in a variety of ways; they discourage employment directly; they reduce profits, which in turn affects investment - the linchpin of forecast growth; and they require monetary policy to be held firmer than otherwise to maintain the two to three percent inflation objective," the RBA said.
"A disappointing aspect of this development is that some wage negotiations seem to have been based on higher inflation than has, in fact, been recorded," the RBA said.
It said wages growth had been consistent with its target level only because a significant part of the labour force has received modest increases.
The RBA said wage outcomes may fall in the coming months with the wider community recognition of lower inflationary expectations.
"Other things equal, a reduction in inflationary expectations would support the case for a reduction in the overnight cash rate," the RBA said.

"Should the economy turn out to be clearly weaker than current projections assume, with likely additional downward pressures on wage bargains and inflation, that case would be strengthened," the bank said.

"On the other hand, on current growth projections, and without evidence that wages are adjusting to the lower inflation environment, a relaxation of monetary policy could have the effect of storing up problems for the future," it said.
The bank said there appeared for room for the economy to grow a little, depending on wages.
"There may be potential for the economy to grow a little faster than at present without threatening inflation, but this depends largely on wage prospects," the bank said.
The RBA said the economy "continues to present a mixed picture, as would be expected from an economy growing somewhere near its long term trend."
"Some sectors are growing quite strongly, but others - manufacturing for example - remain listless," it said.
"Employment growth, while strong enough to absorb new entrants to the labour force, has not made inroads into unemployment over the past year," the bank said.
